extraction.name: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text
extraction.description: The Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) is a reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage. The dataset is designed to evaluate machine reading comprehension and contains 107,785 question-answer pairs on 536 articles, covering a wide range of topics.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.citeAs: Rajpurkar, P., Zhang, J., Lopyrev, K., & Liang, P. (2016). SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. arXiv:1606.05250.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: (1) Passage curation: High-quality Wikipedia articles were selected using Project Nayuki's internal PageRanks, and paragraphs were extracted, stripped of images/tables, and filtered by length. (2) Question-answer collection: Crowdworkers on the Daemo platform (using Amazon Mechanical Turk) created questions and answers on the curated paragraphs, with specific guidelines and examples provided. (3) Additional answers collection: Additional answers were obtained for questions in the development and test sets to assess human performance and improve evaluation robustness.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Crowdsourcing, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles, specifically paragraphs extracted from the top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles ranked by internal PageRanks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Paragraphs were extracted from Wikipedia articles, stripped of images, figures, tables, and filtered to exclude paragraphs shorter than 500 characters. The dataset was partitioned into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions per paragraph, with answers required to be highlighted segments of text from the paragraph. Additional answers were collected for questions in the development and test sets to assess human performance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform (with Amazon Mechanical Turk as backend)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Additional answers were collected for questions in the development and test sets to assess human performance and improve evaluation robustness. 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 additional answers per question in the development and test sets (beyond the initial crowdworker-generated answers).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is freely available and has been updated since its initial release (e.g., SQuAD v1.1). The authors encourage exploration of more expressive models and expect further improvements in model performance.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases inherent in Wikipedia articles, such as overrepresentation of certain topics or perspectives. Additionally, the crowdworker-generated questions and answers may reflect biases in the crowdworkers' backgrounds or interpretations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to questions whose answers are entailed by the passage, and answers are constrained to spans within the passage. The dataset does not include interpretative or free-form questions, which may limit its applicability to certain types of reading comprehension tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation for machine reading comprehension models. The dataset is designed to evaluate and improve models for reading comprehension tasks, with potential applications in natural language understanding and question-answering systems.
